subject.title: [Feature]: Support sessionKey-based concurrency guard for webhook       deliveries

question: Should same-session hook-agent deliveries be rejected with 409, skipped, queued, or left accepted by default, and should any non-parallel behavior be opt-in per hook or mapping?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix changes public webhook response semantics, retry behavior, and session-state policy, so automation should not choose reject/skip/queue/default compatibility without maintainer intent.

options.title: Add Opt-In Overlap Policy
options.body: Keep current accepted-by-default behavior and add a documented hook or mapping policy for reject, skip, or queue semantics keyed by the resolved `sessionKey`.

options.title: Make 409 The Default
options.body: Reject active same-session hook deliveries by default and accept that existing webhook integrations may need migration to avoid retry storms.

options.title: Fold Into Webhook Queues
options.body: Let the broader queued-webhook design own same-session concurrency, then narrow this issue after that design explicitly covers reject or skip behavior.

recommendation.title: Add Opt-In Overlap Policy
recommendation.body: Keep current accepted-by-default behavior and add a documented hook or mapping policy for reject, skip, or queue semantics keyed by the resolved `sessionKey`.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has prior product-boundary history on webhook mappings and hook session behavior, while the unresolved choice is public Gateway API compatibility rather than a single-line code owner question.
